title: Browser Game Not Loading on Your Phone? 7 Checks Before You Reset Anything
excerpt: A practical checklist for browser games that freeze, show a blank screen or lose progress, including what to check before clearing site data.
content:
A browser game that goes blank is not automatically broken for everyone. The problem can sit in the game service, the browser, the network or saved data on your phone. Start by narrowing it down before deleting anything.

This checklist is for web games, including the kind covered in our Lagos Life guide and Danfo Run explainer. It does not claim that either game currently has an outage, or that we reproduced a particular fault.

1. Record what fails

Note the exact address, the time, your phone model and browser. Does the page open but the game stay black? Does the start button do nothing? Does progress disappear after a reload? Those are different symptoms. A short description will help the developer more than “it is not working.” Avoid including passwords or private account details in screenshots.

2. Open the official link in a full browser

If you arrived through a social app, copy the official game address into your normal browser. This is a comparison test: if the same link works there, the problem may involve the in-app browser. Check the address against the creator's own page before trying a replacement link sent by a stranger.

3. Check whether other sites work

Open a familiar site, then try the game once on another connection if one is available. Record which combination works. This does not prove the cause, but separates an all-sites connection problem from a single-service problem. Repeatedly refreshing a page during a service outage is unlikely to provide useful evidence.

4. Restart the browser and reduce competing tabs

Save anything important, close the game tab and reopen it. Then try with fewer tabs and other demanding apps open. Change one thing at a time so you know which change mattered. Mozilla includes restarting among its browser troubleshooting steps.

5. Compare another browser

Use a browser already installed on your device if possible. If only one browser fails, note its version and whether content-blocking tools are active. On desktop Firefox, Mozilla's troubleshooting mode can help isolate extensions and other settings. Do not switch off all security protections just to make an unfamiliar game run.

6. Treat clearing data as a later step

Mozilla also recommends cookies and cache checks for page-loading problems. Before clearing a game's stored data, check whether your progress is linked to an account or only saved in that browser. Clearing local information may remove progress that has no server copy. Prefer a targeted site-data action over wiping every site's sessions.

7. Send a useful report

Share the official URL, browser version, symptom and the comparison results with the creator's published support channel. Say whether a different browser or connection worked. Never give someone your password to “repair” your save.

What this checklist can and cannot establish

These steps help isolate a fault; they cannot repair a game server or guarantee recovery of a local save. For more games in this category, see our Nigerian browser-game roundup.

Research note: based on browser support documentation, checked 10 October 2026. No live game outage or device-specific fix was independently tested for this article.

title: Refurbished Phone Buying Checklist: Battery, Locks and Returns
excerpt: Check battery promises, network compatibility, condition grades, accessories and return terms before choosing a refurbished phone.
content:
The cheapest refurbished phone is only a good buy if it can do what you need and you have a workable route back to the seller when something is wrong. Compare the exact listing rather than assuming every device carrying the word refurbished has the same standard.

For the marketplace model itself, start with our Back Market explainer. This article is a buying checklist, not a review of a handset we purchased.

Separate appearance from battery condition

A neat-looking phone and a healthy battery answer different questions. Ask what minimum battery capacity is promised and whether the listing offers a replacement battery. Do not interpret an appearance grade as a battery test result unless the seller explicitly connects them.

For example, Back Market's US Premium-device policy describes a minimum 90% battery capacity and genuine manufacturer parts for that specific tier. That is not a promise covering every seller's refurbished phone or every grade. Save the listing you actually order.

Match the exact model to your network

Write down the model identifier, storage size and whether it is unlocked. If you plan to use it in Nigeria or another country, check the exact variant with your mobile network rather than relying on the broad product name. Ask whether it uses a physical SIM, eSIM or both. A lower price is less useful if your intended connection will not work.

Confirm locks and ownership before payment

Ask the seller to confirm that the phone will arrive ready for your own account, without an old owner's activation lock or an organisation's management restriction. If a private seller cannot demonstrate this, pause the transaction. Make the requirement explicit in writing so there is a clear record of what was promised.

Check what is included

Budget for accessories as part of the total cost. Back Market's accessory guidance says smartphone orders include a compatible charging cable, while wall chargers and earphones are not included. Other sellers can have different bundles. Check the product page instead of assuming a sealed-box experience.

Read the return route as carefully as the warranty

A warranty period alone does not tell you who pays shipping or how a claim is handled. Record the seller, support channel, return window, exclusions and where the phone must be sent. The US Premium page states a 30-day change-of-mind policy and a seller's one-year limited warranty. Those are scoped US terms; check the country and current listing before relying on them.

Keep a short arrival checklist

  1. Photograph the packaging and compare the model and condition with your saved order.
  2. Set up your own account and test your intended SIM or connection.
  3. Check charging, cameras, speakers, microphone, screen and buttons.
  4. Record any fault promptly using the seller's stated support process.

This is a practical inspection plan, not proof of laboratory testing or a guarantee against hidden faults. If your priority is repair access rather than the lowest purchase price, our Fairphone article explains another approach to phone ownership.

Research note: seller documentation checked 10 October 2026. No handset was bought or tested for this article; country-specific terms may differ.

title: Booking.com Free Cancellation: Which Deadline Actually Applies?
excerpt: Find the cancellation deadline for your exact Booking.com rate, understand Partner Offers and keep the confirmation evidence you need.
content:
Free cancellation on Booking.com is a condition of the particular offer you book, not a single deadline applied to every hotel. Two rates for the same room can have different rules. The useful question is: what did the confirmation for my exact booking say?

Our Booking.com explainer covers the platform and its business model. This guide focuses on reading a cancellation policy.

Start with the rate, not the property headline

Before paying, inspect the chosen room and rate's conditions. Record whether cancellation is free, partly refundable or non-refundable, and the displayed deadline. Keep the date, time and any stated time zone together. “Free cancellation available” somewhere on a property page is not enough to establish the terms of a different rate.

Booking.com's customer terms say cancellation and no-show charges depend on the service provider's policy. They identify the booking flow, property information and confirmation as places those policies appear. The same hotel name therefore does not establish identical refund terms.

Save the confirmation before you need it

Keep the confirmation email or download a copy. A useful record includes the property, stay dates, room, rate terms and booking reference. Keep a screenshot of the displayed deadline if it helps. These records let you ask a precise question if the charge or cancellation outcome differs from what you expected.

Check whether it is a Partner Offer

Booking.com's Partner Offer help page describes offers facilitated through partner travel companies, with restrictions on changes. Read that section if your reservation carries the Partner Offer label. Its rules should not be applied to every ordinary reservation on the platform.

A practical check before buying is to ask whether your plans could change. If flexibility matters, compare the actual flexible offer and its final price instead of assuming customer support can later turn a restricted offer into one that allows changes.

Distinguish a request from confirmation

Use the cancellation route in the booking confirmation or your account, then retain the resulting cancellation acknowledgement. Booking.com's Partner Offer help page says a cancellation email should follow a completed cancellation. If the status is unclear, contact support through the official booking rather than assuming that an unanswered message to a property changed the reservation.

Do not substitute another hotel's refund timeline

Keep policy eligibility, cancellation confirmation and the arrival of money in your account as separate questions. Identify who collected the payment and use the support route relevant to your booking. We have not tested a refund, and there is no universal arrival date asserted here.

A short pre-booking record

  • Exact room and rate selected.
  • Cancellation deadline with its displayed time zone.
  • Fee after that deadline and no-show terms.
  • Payment collection details and any Partner Offer label.
  • A saved confirmation and official support route.

This checklist helps you avoid guessing from general advertising. For another platform's model, read our Agoda explainer and compare the actual offers rather than brand names alone.

Research note: official terms and help pages checked 10 October 2026. No reservation or refund was tested; this is an explanation of published platform information.

title: Data Removal vs VPN: What Each Privacy Tool Can Actually Do
excerpt: A VPN changes how a connection travels. Data removal targets broker records. Understand the difference before choosing a privacy subscription.
content:
A VPN and a data-removal service address different parts of your online exposure. A VPN can protect the connection between your device and its server. A removal service tries to get personal records removed from the organisations it covers. Buying one does not automatically give you the other.

Our Incogni explainer describes the removal-service model. Our Surfshark VPN article covers the connection tool. This comparison helps you decide which question you need answered first.

What a VPN changes

Surfshark's encryption explanation describes an encrypted connection between your device and a VPN server. That addresses traffic on that connection. It does not itself send deletion requests to a people-search site that already lists your address.

Consider an everyday example: you turn on a VPN, then visit a site where you are signed into your own account. Changing the route of the connection does not turn that account into an unknown person. Treat claims of complete anonymity cautiously and ask which part of the system a tool actually changes.

What data removal targets

Incogni's opt-out guides describe identifying brokers, following each site's removal process and checking again because records may return. This targets stored information at particular organisations. It does not replace connection encryption.

Manual removal can be a starting point when you know which listing concerns you. A paid service may help with repeated requests, but the covered brokers, supported regions and current subscription terms matter more than a broad claim to remove you from the internet.

Use an exposure list before choosing a subscription

Make a private list of what you want to address: a visible people-search record, an old public profile, recurring messages, or concern about a network connection. Do not publish that list. Identify the organisation holding the record and the official support or removal route. If the problem is a public profile you control, start with its own visibility and account settings.

Questions to ask a removal provider

  • Does it cover the organisation that holds the record?
  • Does it support where you live?
  • What personal details must you provide to identify the record?
  • How does it show completed requests and unsuccessful ones?
  • Does it recheck, and what continues after cancellation?

These are comparison questions, not a finding that every provider supplies all those features. Ask for the current written terms.

A simple comparison

If your question is “how does this connection travel?”, investigate the VPN's scope. If it is “why is this broker listing my details?”, investigate the holder's removal process. If it is “why am I receiving suspicious messages?”, also check account security and the original source of the messages; neither product should be assumed to solve that entire problem.

Research note: provider documentation checked 10 October 2026. No subscription effectiveness, regional eligibility or removal outcome was independently tested. Provider descriptions are not a comparative performance endorsement.

title: Etsy Seller Asking You to Pay Elsewhere? What to Check
excerpt: Learn why an off-platform payment request changes your Etsy protection and how to check messages without following a suspicious link.
content:
If an Etsy seller asks you to finish a purchase through a separate payment link or private chat, pause before paying. A listing on Etsy does not make a payment elsewhere an Etsy transaction. Check where the checkout actually happens and which protections apply.

Our Etsy marketplace explainer covers the platform. This article focuses on off-platform payment requests and messages that impersonate support.

Keep the proposed payment and the original order separate

Read the request carefully. Is the seller answering a product question, or asking you to replace the platform checkout with a different payment? A normal conversation about an item and a new request for money are not the same event. Do not let an existing order make every later payment request feel automatically legitimate.

Etsy's off-platform scam guidance warns that purchases moved away from its platform cannot rely on Etsy Purchase Protection. It tells buyers to avoid payment requests that bypass its checkout. That does not mean every on-platform order has an unconditional refund: the protection programme has its own eligibility rules.

Check the request inside the account

Open the Etsy app or type the known site address yourself, then inspect your messages and order. This gives you a separate path to the account instead of relying entirely on a link supplied by the sender. If the claimed problem or order cannot be located there, ask through the official account support route before taking action.

A support-looking name is not enough

Etsy's phishing guidance describes official messages in the From Etsy inbox with a corresponding badge. It also says Etsy will not ask for your password in Messages. Check those account indicators rather than trusting a sender who simply puts Etsy or Support into a display name.

Use the pressure test

Ask yourself what would happen if you waited long enough to check the account properly. A sender's urgency is not proof that the request is legitimate. Keep a record of the message and the proposed destination, but do not scan an unexpected code, share a verification code or enter account details on a page reached only through that message.

Report the message through the platform

For suspicious Messages, Etsy's guidance recommends reporting instead of replying. Use the reporting controls in your account. A useful private record includes the account name, the order it claimed to concern and a screenshot of the request. Remove private details before showing screenshots publicly.

What to check on your next order

  • The item, variation, price and delivery estimate match what you intended to buy.
  • The payment stays in the platform's authorised purchase flow.
  • Product questions and transaction evidence stay with the order.
  • You understand the applicable return and purchase-protection conditions.

No seller account was investigated for this article, and no purchase was made. The goal is to recognise a change in the transaction route early enough to check it. Our AliExpress explainer provides another marketplace model to compare; its rules must be checked separately.

Research note: Etsy's official help pages checked 10 October 2026. This article explains platform guidance and does not promise reimbursement for an individual order.
